units: <cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 1:1">B. Kam. I, 1</cite> <he>תַּשְׁלוּמֵי נזק</he>, v. <cite ref="N00461"><he>נֵזֶק</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 1:2">Ib. 2</cite> <he>חבתי בת׳</he> (Y. a. Bab. ed. 9ᵇ <he>בתשלומי נזקו</he>), v. <cite ref="H00231"><he>חוּב</he></cite> h. Ib. 3 <he>הניזק והמזיק בת׳</he> the injured and the injurer may be subject to payment of indemnities; Tosef. ib. I, 3 <he>הניזק … בת׳ לשלם חצי נזק</he> they may be subject to payment in the event of half-damage having to be paid (v. Bab. ib. 15ᵃ).

<cite ref="Tosefta Ketubot 3:5">Tosef. Keth. III, 5</cite> <he>יום הכפורים הרי הוא כשבת לת׳</he> the Day of Atonement is like the Sabbath with regard to indemnification; <cite ref="Ketubot 30a:5">Keth. 30ᵃ</cite> <he>מה שבת … ופטור מן הת׳ וכ׳</he> as he who does forbidden labor on the Sabbath forfeits his life, and is exempt from indemnity (if he did damage through his labor), so he &c. Sifra Emor Par. 14, ch. XX (ref. to <cite ref="Leviticus 24:21">Lev. XXIV, 21</cite>) <he>מה מכה בהמה בת׳ אף … בת׳</he> as he who injures an animal pays damages, so he who injures a man has to pay an indemnity for the injured limb. Y. B. Bab. II, end, 3ᵃ <he>וייעשה מי שחלו עליו ת׳</he> let him be treated as one on whom rests the obligation to pay damages. Ib. <he>על … נתחייב מיתה מכאן והילך ת׳</he> let him be guilty of death for the first ear of corn (which he ignited on the Sabbath), and guilty of damages for the rest; a. fr.
Ker. 27ᵃ, v. next w.—Pl. as ab.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 2:5:3">Y. Erub. II, 20ᵇ</cite> <he>מטלטלין בשני ת׳ לראשון</he> you may move things (on the Sabbath) within the second partition as far as would make up the legally allowed distance for the first partition.
